idea: D-004 (operator direction, supersedes prior D-001): make ONE persistent daemon the sole owner/writer of crews' durable coordination files, with members talking to it over IPC instead of file-locks + per-process hooks. Preserve Layer B durability (cursor + audit history + operator review-gates + crash-recovery) while eliminating the lock-contention (EPERM/LockTimeout) and hook fragility. Codex-only members acceptable. Daemon vehicle: codex app-server if feasible on Windows, else the happy-cli daemon, else a small dedicated sidecar.

candidateDirections.name: Happy-cli daemon owns Layer-B state + a THIN codex hook for the hard gate
candidateDirections.summary: happy-cli 127.0.0.1 daemon becomes the single-writer owner of crews' coordination state (kills the multi-process locks; substrate ~80% shipped as agent-comms Scope B), while a thin codex Stop/PreToolUse hook that does zero file I/O keeps querying the daemon to preserve the hard decision:block turn-veto. Recommended PARTIAL->GO path.

candidateDirections.name: Pure daemon, NO per-process hooks (operator's literal wish) with explicit acceptance the hard gate degrades to advisory
candidateDirections.summary: Members run with ZERO hooks; the daemon enforces review server-side by refusing the next IPC op + a between-turns MCP wake. Fully grants the verbatim wish but LOSES the hard turn-block (only a Stop hook can veto a codex turn-end), so adopt only with knowing operator acceptance of a soft/advisory gate.

candidateDirections.name: Point-fix crews' Windows lock sites; question whether a daemon is needed at all
candidateDirections.summary: Avoid a second-system rewrite: share-delete manifest reads to kill the reader-rename race, an in-process write-queue for the lead, and lean on the fact codex-only migration already shrinks N. Corroborated by prior-brainstorm D-003 + durable-mailbox-channel-wake.md §3 (which already rejected moving crews storage off the filesystem mailbox).

candidateDirections.name: Codex app-server itself as the coordination daemon (NO-GO on Windows now)
candidateDirections.summary: Answers the operator's 'app server if possible?' explicitly: ruled out today because the Rust app-server-daemon is Unix-only, its websocket transport is experimental/unsupported, and the happy-cli app-server client is one-thread-per-process / one-server-per-cwd. Revisit only if codex ships supported Windows daemon lifecycle + durable multi-client coordination + a hard turn-complete policy hook.

questionsForSynthesis: Does the operator ACCEPT downgrading the hard turn-block (Stop decision:block) to a cooperative/advisory daemon gate (-> D-002), or is hard parity required (-> D-001 thin hook)? This single decision picks the direction.

Forensics: do the EPERM/LockTimeout incidents originate in concurrent WRITES (a single-writer daemon fixes these) or concurrent manifest READS (the FILE_SHARE_DELETE rename race at pre-tool-use.js:583, which needs single-ACCESSOR)? Decides the rewrite size.
Must history.jsonl become fail-loud (it is best-effort today at mailbox.ts:255-266) before crews audit behavior is retired?
Who owns the daemon's Windows lifecycle (start-on-login, crash-restart, supervised service), and is the daemon-SPOF blast radius acceptable vs today's localized per-member lock contention?
Is cross-engine loss (Claude/Copilot members) fully accepted for ralph brainstorm/plan lenses too, or only for routine members?
